encounters.cc: Progressive difficulty swallowing with sensation of food slowing behind lower sternum

lines: Progressive difficulty swallowing with sensation of food slowing behind lower sternum
He describes the sensation that both solid foods and liquids seem to slow down behind the lower part of his breast bone shortly after eating.
He sometimes regurgitates undigested food but denies weight loss, chest pain, or heartburn.
He has no prior upper gastrointestinal procedures
He takes only a statin for hyperlipidemia.
He does not smoke or drink alcohol.
A barium swallow is shown below.

encounters.cc: Progressive dyspnea on exertion and bilateral lower extremity edema over 6 months

lines: Progressive dyspnea on exertion and bilateral lower extremity edema over 6 months
The patient with Parkinson disease, evaluated six months prior for dysphagia, presents to clinic with a 6-month history of progressive dyspnea on exertion and bilateral lower extremity edema.
His past medical history is significant for carpal tunnel syndrome,.
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
On physical examination, his blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg, heart rate is 92 beats per minute,
Cardiac auscultation reveals a third heart sound (S3) but no murmurs.
Lung fields are clear to auscultation.
- Urinalysis: 3+ protein, no blood or casts
Echocardiogram: Increased left ventricular wall thickness with normal left ventricular cavity size, preserved ejection fraction, and speckled appearance of the myocardium
Electrocardiogram (ECG): Low voltage QRS complexes and diffuse nonspecific ST-T wave abnormalities

encounters.cc: Continued difficulty with fine motor movements and facial expressiveness despite medication compliance

lines: Continued difficulty with fine motor movements and facial expressiveness despite medication compliance
This 68-year-old male with Parkinson disease, achalasia, and cardiac amyloidosis returns for follow-up of his movement disorder.
His caregiver reports that he often hesitates when initiating motion and frequently appears stiff, especially in the morning and late in the day.
Although he had some initial benefit from therapy started months ago, she feels his condition has plateaued and remains functionally limiting.
- Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) with left internal mammary artery harvest
He has been consistently taking a combination medication containing levodopa and carbidopa.
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
His appetite is preserved and he sleeps through most nights.
There is no report of muscle weakness or memory impairment, and he remains independent in basic daily needs.
Physical exam reveals slowed finger tapping, a low-volume voice, and reduced swing in the right arm while walking.
His mood is subdued but cooperative, and his vitals are within normal limits.
Basic labs including thyroid panel and metabolic profile are unremarkable.
A plan is made to adjust his regimen by adding a second medication targeting a different enzymatic mechanism.

encounters.cc: Persistent bleeding from chest tube and oozing around central line site following CABG

lines: Persistent bleeding from chest tube and oozing around central line site following CABG

The patient is a 70-year-old male with a history of Parkinson disease, transthyretin wild-type cardiac amyloidosis diagnosed in 2020, and achalasia who undergoes coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) for severe multivessel coronary artery disease.
The surgery is uneventful, and he is transferred to the cardiac ICU on mechanical ventilation.
Two hours later, the surgical team is called to the bedside because of persistent bleeding from the chest tube and oozing around the central line site.
The patient has received several liters of IV fluids and blood products, but the bleeding continues.
He had been anticoagulated intraoperatively with intravenous unfractionated heparin to maintain cardiopulmonary bypass.
- Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) with left internal mammary artery harvest
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
Postoperative labs reveal prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT), normal prothrombin time (PT), normal platelet count, and normal fibrinogen.
There is no evidence of thrombocytopenia or disseminated intravascular coagulation.
The surgical team suspects continued anticoagulation as the cause of bleeding and requests urgent reversal.

encounters.cc: Mild chest pain and sensation of chest wall 'popping' with movement for 2 days

lines: Mild chest pain and sensation of chest wall 'popping' with movement for 2 days
He underwent coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) 3 weeks ago.
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
He denies fever, cough, or shortness of breath.
On examination, his temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, and respiratory rate is 16/min.
Cardiovascular examination reveals a well-healed median sternotomy scar.
Palpation of the chest wall elicits a 'clicking' sensation and the patient reports discomfort.
There is no erythema or purulent discharge from the incision site.
A chest X-ray shows a displaced sternal wire.

encounters.cc: Fever, malaise, and increasing redness and pain around sternal wound 10 days post-CABG

lines: Fever, malaise, and increasing redness and pain around sternal wound 10 days post-CABG

This patient with known cardiac amyloidosis and Parkinson disease presents to the emergency department 10 days post-coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), having recently been evaluated for wound dehiscence.
He reports a low-grade fever started 3 days ago, which has progressively worsened.
- Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) with left internal mammary artery harvest
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
On examination, his temperature is 38.9°C (102°F), heart rate is 110 bpm, and blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg.
The sternal wound is erythematous with some purulent discharge.
There is notable swelling and tenderness to palpation over the sternum.
A chest X-ray reveals a small fluid collection anterior to the sternum.

encounters.cc: Difficulty breathing when lying flat and fatigue on exertion with paradoxical abdominal motion

lines: Difficulty breathing when lying flat and fatigue on exertion with paradoxical abdominal motion

This 70-year-old male with Parkinson disease, transthyretin wild-type cardiac amyloidosis, and recent coronary artery bypass grafting complicated by mediastinitis presents to the Pulmonology clinic with difficulty breathing, especially when lying flat, and fatigue on exertion that has progressively worsened over the past two months.
He reports a sensation of his abdomen moving inward when he takes a deep breath.
His past medical history is significant for coronary artery disease,.
For which he underwent coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgery three months ago.
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
On physical examination, you observe that his abdomen indeed moves inward during inspiration, and auscultation of the lungs reveals decreased breath sounds at the left lung base.
- Arterial blood gas on room air:
Chest x-ray shows an elevated left hemidiaphragm.

encounters.cc: Acute onset visual hallucinations and paranoid ideation accusing neighbors of stealing

lines: Acute onset visual hallucinations and paranoid ideation accusing neighbors of stealing

The patient is a 72-year-old male with Parkinson disease, transthyretin wild-type cardiac amyloidosis status post complicated coronary artery bypass grafting, and achalasia, returning for evaluation and presents to the clinic with his wife, who reports that over the past month, he has been experiencing visual hallucinations and has become increasingly paranoid, accusing neighbors of stealing from him.
The patient has been on a stable regimen of carbidopa/levodopa and pramipexole.
His symptoms are well controlled, and he denies any recent changes in his motor function.
- Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) with left internal mammary artery harvest
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
His vital signs are within normal limits.
On examination, the patient is alert and oriented to person, place, and time.
Neurological examination reveals a resting tremor, bradykinesia, and rigidity consistent with his known Parkinson disease.
There are no signs of infection or delirium.
